questions.prompt: How is tempo typically expressed in the lecture’s notation example?
choices: A Only with Italian adjectives and never numbers.
B Beats per minute (BPM), e.g. quarter note = 60 (one pulse per second).
C As the number of ledger lines on the staff.
D Exclusively as asymmetric meters.
questions.explain: Tempo as BPM: crotchet/quarter = 60 means 60 pulses per minute.

questions.prompt: What is true of a grace note in his account?
choices: A It always counts as a full eighth note inside the 4/4 total.
B It typically precedes the main beat, often slurred, and does not count as a definite beat value toward the meter.
C It replaces the time signature.
D It can only appear after the final double bar.
questions.explain: Grace notes (small head, slash) precede the main note and aren’t counted like ordinary eighths in the bar’s arithmetic.

questions.prompt: Binary form, in his large-scale discussion, is described as:
choices: A An endless development with no sections.
B An AB form—among the simplest directional musical forms.
C Only possible with twelve-tone rows.
D Identical to a five-movement symphony cycle.
questions.explain: He introduces binary form as AB—simple directional large-scale form.

questions.prompt: In sonata-allegro exposition, what typically happens after the first theme on the tonic?
choices: A Immediate coda in the parallel minor with no transition.
B A transition often toward the dominant, laying out thematic materials and harmonic trajectory (often repeated).
C Only percussion solos.
D Abandonment of all themes until the recapitulation.
questions.explain: Exposition: tonic first theme, transition (often to dominant), materials laid out; often repeated after a double bar.

questions.prompt: ABA song-like forms are also known in the Germanic tradition as:
choices: A Only ritornello forms of the Baroque concerto.
B Lied forms (Lieder)—common patterning for German art song.
C Strict serial matrices.
D Mensural colorations.
questions.explain: ABA forms = Lied forms in the Germanic tradition (Schubert, Schumann, Wolf, etc.).
